skill.description: Guides Expo app releases with EAS builds, submissions, metadata, workflows, and store rollout steps.

skill.author: expo

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples, placeholders, or user-run Expo and EAS commands rather than hidden skill behavior. No evidence found of prompt injection, automatic command execution, credential exfiltration, or malicious network use in the cited files. The credential examples are legitimate but should keep strong warnings about secret storage.

remediation.issue: Credential examples may be copied into real projects without enough caution.
remediation.suggestion: Add consistent warnings near Apple and Google credential snippets to never commit key files, prefer EAS Secrets, and rotate exposed keys.

remediation.issue: Placeholder URLs, IDs, and contact fields may be copied unchanged.
remediation.suggestion: Label example values as placeholders and remind users to replace them before submitting store metadata.

content.value_statement: Expo releases require platform-specific build, credential, and store submission steps. This skill guides EAS builds, submissions, metadata, workflows, and rollout planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides EAS CLI setup and eas.json build profile configuration.
Explains iOS builds, App Store Connect submissions, and TestFlight release paths.
Explains Android Play Store submissions, service accounts, tracks, and staged rollout settings.
Provides App Store metadata and ASO guidance for EAS Metadata workflows.
Shows EAS Workflows patterns for web deploys, previews, builds, and submissions.
limitations: Does not run deployment commands automatically.
Requires valid Expo, Apple Developer, and Google Play Console access.
Requires project-specific credentials, bundle identifiers, and store records.
Store policies and EAS behavior can change, so official documentation should be checked.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First Mobile Release
use_cases.description: Plan the EAS setup, production build profile, and store submission sequence for a new Expo app.

use_cases.title: Automate Release Workflows
use_cases.description: Design build, submit, preview, and production deployment workflows for a team release process.

use_cases.title: Improve Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Review app metadata, rollout settings, track choices, and common rejection risks before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First EAS Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an Expo project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare my Expo app for a first EAS production build. List the setup steps, required accounts, and checks before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Store Submission
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate iOS and Android release preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Expo release plan for App Store and Play Store submission. Identify missing credentials, metadata, store records, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Release Tracks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release-track plan for my Expo app. Include TestFlight, Play internal testing, staged rollout, and production release criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design Automated Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an EAS Workflows strategy for builds, PR previews, web deploys, store submissions, and version management for a team Expo project.

output_examples.input: I need to release my Expo app to both stores for the first time.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering account setup, production profiles, credential readiness, build commands, store records, review information, and final submission order.

output_examples.input: Our team wants automated previews and tagged production releases.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan that separates pull request previews, web deployment, native builds, store submissions, and approval checkpoints.

output_examples.input: My Android release needs a safer rollout.
output_examples.output: A staged rollout recommendation with internal testing first, track selection, service account checks, and monitoring steps after submission.

best_practices: Use EAS Secrets or protected CI variables for store credentials.
Start releases with internal testing before production rollout.
Verify store metadata, privacy details, and version numbers before submission.
anti_patterns: Committing service account keys or Apple private key files to source control.
Submitting directly to production before TestFlight or internal track validation.
Copying placeholder bundle identifiers, app IDs, URLs, or contact details unchanged.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy my app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You decide when to run EAS commands.

faq.question: Does it cover both iOS and Android releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers App Store, TestFlight, Play Store, release tracks, credentials, and submission commands.

faq.question: Does it explain web deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes EAS Hosting and workflow patterns for production deploys and previews.

faq.question: Does it include credential guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Apple and Google credential setup, with recommendations to protect secret files.

faq.question: Can it replace official store documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a workflow guide and verify current requirements with Expo, Apple, and Google documentation.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Expo developers, release engineers, and product teams preparing mobile or web deployments.
